summary: Cast-iron tower on a caisson off Kent Island marking Eastern Bay, lit 1882, gutted by fire in 1960, replaced by a Coast Guard warning light in 2018.

structures.material: cast-iron tower lined with brick on a cast-iron cylinder over a wooden caisson

staffing.note: Keepers until the 1960 fire; a lamp and acrylic lens were installed and the station automated in fall 1961.

access.note: Reached by boat only; not open to the public.

facts.agency: U.S. Coast Guard (owner in 1996); sold at GSA auction 2006; current owner not confirmed in the sources read

events.note: Congress appropriates $25,000 for a lighthouse and fog bell on 3 March 1881
Caisson and cast-iron tower erected from June to August 1882
First exhibited 1 October 1882 with a fourth-order Fresnel lens
Tilt after gales. The Coast Guard nomination dates the gales to 29 February and 3 March 1884; LighthouseFriends and the Chapter timeline say winter 1883
Sand dredged in November 1884; 760 tons of stone laid as a scour apron in spring 1885
Changed from fixed red to fixed white with a red sector over the Poplar Island shoals, 15 April 1888
Fog bell striking machine replaced; copper smoke pipe renewed
Soundings around the light and various repairs
Keepers take in Mrs. Carl J. Hammersla and eight others from a stranded 45-foot boat
Electrical fire on 30 April 1960 gutted the wooden interior; the two Coast Guardsmen on duty escaped by boat
Original fourth-order lens lost in the fire
Lamp and 300 mm acrylic lens installed in fall 1961; station automated
Sold at a General Services Administration online auction; Michael Gabriel of Nevada bought it for $100,000
Large section of the tower broken off, exposing the interior; photographed in 2017, damage dated by LighthouseFriends to more than a year earlier
Coast Guard completed Bloody Point Bar Warning Light in early 2018 to replace the lighthouse

notes_for_editor: Characteristic: the record's Fl W 6s and 7 nm range are not confirmed by any source read; LighthouseFriends describes a fixed white light with a red sector since 1888, and a current Light List check is needed. Focal height 16.5 m matches the archive's 54 ft. NRHP 02001416 (record): the nomination PDF on npgallery is a non-document placeholder in the cache, and the 1996 evaluation records the station as previously determined eligible but finds it not eligible; the listing status is unverified. Ownership: Coast Guard in 1996; GSA auction and sale to Michael Gabriel in 2006 per LighthouseFriends; the owner today is not confirmed. The 2018 warning light date rests on LighthouseFriends ('early 2018'); a Coast Guard Sector Maryland post dated 1 February 2018 was seen only as a search snippet and the page could not be opened, so it is not cited. The fire: the nomination says propane tanks, LighthouseFriends a 500-gallon fuel tank. Storm year: winter 1883 (LighthouseFriends, Chapter timeline) against 29 February and 3 March 1884 (nomination); tilt five feet (LighthouseFriends) against about six degrees (nomination). 1939 rescue: LighthouseFriends names Hiram White as keeper and Louis Carmen as his assistant; the archive roster has Lewis R. Carman as head keeper and White as first assistant; the story gives both. 1948: the Sun article names keeper Tom White, who does not appear on the archive roster (which has Leslie F. Garrish as head keeper 1947 to 1950); White is not linked to Hiram T. White. The Chesapeake Chapter keeper bios were not checked for this station. The Chronicling America search for the 1939 rescue returned no hit, and the 1960 search returned unrelated pages, so no newspaper is cited. Ages of the 1960 Coast Guardsmen are left out. Roster person slugs came from roster.py --json.
